chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who is given goods (or a loan of items), and it is said to him, 'What I have added to [the value/quantity of] such and such is for you.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: Goods, items, or movable property given for use or trade
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to agree that profit or increase from rented goods belongs to the owner?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on rentals (al-Ijarat) in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of a specific profit-sharing or rental agreement where the lessee retains any surplus value generated from the goods. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of flexibility in commercial contracts, provided the core terms are clear and no prohibited elements (gharar) are present. The ruling underscores the Imam’s approval of practical economic arrangements that facilitate trade while maintaining fairness.
